Financial Reforms
An efficient system of taxation was introduced in which the rich were taxed more
thanthepoor.
Agricultural area was increased for better crop output.
Indian peasants were required to pay about one-third of their annual harvest to the
state, but the system was applied justly. When bad weather struck in the 1590s,
taxes werereduced or suspended altogether.
Trade and manufacturing industry flourished. Indian goods, especially textiles,
exchange for gold and silver.
Mansabdari System
In 1570 AD, Mansabdari System was introduced as a new administrative and revenue
system. Mansabdars were directly accountable to the emperor. They were responsible to
collect theland revenue and all other taxes,Militaryresponsibilities of Mansabdars were
to maintain a specified number of cavalrymen, to get them registered and their horses
trademarked.This was meant to reinforce the emperor's military power during wars.
Religious Reforms
Akbar followed liberal views towards religion. He used to hold discussions with the
leaders of different religions.Akbar adopted a policy of religious tolerance based on
honesty,justice,and peace.Hebelievedthat all religions taught similar beliefs and ideals.
Abul Fazl, Akbar'sfriend and counsellor, helped Akbar in framing the idea of one common
religion so that he could govern a diverse Indian
society effectively and peacefully. Indeed,Akbar
incorporated the principles of different religions to
found a new faith which he named Din-i-llahi.
Muslims clergy completely disapproved of Akbar's
newreligion.Din-i-llahi'did not attract many converts
anditperishedwiththedeathofAkbar.
